checks.check: two monitors, the first one primary
the second monitor lies right of the first
the taskbar of monitor 2 is a 48 px dock at its bottom, as wide as the monitor
it is on monitor 2, above the windows, on every workspace and out of the window list
one taskbar window per other monitor only
the panel window covers monitor 1 (the primary)
monitor 2 has a strut: its work area ends above its taskbar
monitor 1 keeps its own strut
the dev state has the taskbar of monitor 2 (tb-strip-m1)
its window is the monitor wide and 48 px high
it has no Start, search, Task View, tray or clock
the main taskbar keeps Start, Task View, the tray and the clock
the taskbar of monitor 2 is frosted like the main one (w11-glass, a strip backdrop)
the desktop window covers monitor 1 (the primary; Mutter keeps a desktop window in one work area)
monitor 2 has a desktop window of its own (SecondaryDesktop.Monitor1, a desktop window on monitor 2)
the desktop geometry lists both monitors with the primary marked
the desktop window of monitor 2 draws the wallpaper over all of it (desktop-wall-1)
monitor 1 shows the whole picture by itself (four colours at 25 %/75 %, in our desktop window there)
monitor 2 shows the whole picture by itself (four colours at 25 %/75 %, in our desktop window there)
span: monitor 1 shows its own part of one picture over both monitors
span: monitor 2 shows its own part of one picture over both monitors
every desktop icon lies on monitor 1 above its taskbar
a right click on the empty desktop of monitor 2 opens the desktop menu there (in its desktop window)
Escape closes the desktop menu
Nieuw > Map on monitor 2 makes the folder on the desktop of monitor 1, its name ready to type
the desktop of monitor 1 has the keyboard now, not the desktop window of monitor 2 that was clicked
the name typed right after goes into it: the folder is called "mmreis"
Task Manager is on monitor 2
by default ("Taskbar where window is open") Task Manager shows on the taskbar of monitor 2 only
Settings on monitor 2: running on its taskbar, the main taskbar keeps its pin without is-running
the taskbar of monitor 2 shows no pins by default
"All taskbars": Task Manager on both taskbars, the pins on monitor 2 too
"Main taskbar and taskbar where window is open": Task Manager on both, no pins on monitor 2
back to the default: on the taskbar of monitor 2 only
moved to monitor 1 it is on the main taskbar and leaves the other
moved back to monitor 2 it is on its taskbar again
the Task Manager button on the taskbar of monitor 2
a click on its button on the taskbar of monitor 2 focuses Task Manager
a second click minimizes it
it minimizes into its button on the taskbar of monitor 2 (icon geometry inside that taskbar)
a third click restores and focuses it
a right click on the button opens its jump list (menus-jump-launch, -pin, -close) on monitor 2
no window list opens over the jump list while the pointer stays on the button
Escape closes it
a right click on its empty space opens the taskbar menu (Taakbeheer, Taakbalkinstellingen)
no window list opens over the taskbar menu while the pointer rests on an app button
Settings has "Show my taskbar on all displays", on and enabled with two displays
and "When using multiple displays, show my taskbar apps on", enabled
"Show my taskbar on all displays" off: the taskbar of monitor 2 is gone
and its strut: the work area of monitor 2 is the whole monitor
the main taskbar shows Task Manager again (every window, as with one monitor)
the second row is greyed out while the first is off
on again: the taskbar of monitor 2 is back
and Task Manager is on it again
locked: no taskbar of monitor 2
after unlock the taskbar of monitor 2 is back at its place
after unlock Task Manager is on it again (and not on the main taskbar)
after unlock both taskbars tell GNOME again where their buttons are (windows.setIconRects; the main taskbar too, whose buttons did not move)
the windows of monitor 2 carry their en titles
after switching to nl the taskbar and desktop windows of monitor 2 have their nl titles
and back in en
the main taskbar moves to the new primary
the other taskbar is io.github.win11shell.SecondaryTaskbar.Monitor0 at the bottom of the other monitor
the desktop (with the icons) moves to the new primary, the other monitor gets its own desktop window
the desktop icons follow the primary
back: the taskbar of monitor 2 is there again
before: Settings minimizes into the main taskbar, Task Manager into the taskbar of monitor 2
monitor 2 left of monitor 1: Settings still minimizes into the main taskbar and Task Manager into the taskbar of its monitor, though neither taskbar changed size
back in the first order: the taskbar of monitor 2 is in its place again
monitor 2 off: no taskbar of another monitor
the desktop covers monitor 1 alone
and no desktop window of another monitor is left
Settings, left open on its Taskbar page, greys both rows out with one display
monitor 2 on again: its taskbar is back
and Settings enables both rows again with two displays
